context.title: David and Goliath
context.summary: For forty days the Philistine champion Goliath defies Israel. David, bringing food to his brothers, is outraged that anyone would defy the living God. Refusing Saul's armor, he faces Goliath with a sling and fells him with one stone.
context.background: The armies faced each other across the valley of Elah, where the Philistine plain meets Judah's hills. The standard Hebrew gives Goliath's height as six cubits and a span, about 9 feet 9 inches; the oldest surviving manuscript of this passage (from the Dead Sea Scrolls) and the Greek translation read four cubits and a span, about 6 feet 9 inches.

customs.note: A thick wooden bar of a loom. Goliath's spear shaft was that heavy, and its iron head alone weighed 600 shekels, about 15 pounds.

watchFor: 'Defy the armies of the living God' (vv. 26, 36).
Saul asks whose son David is (vv. 55–58), though David had served him in chapter 16, a puzzle readers have long discussed.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Saul
people.summary: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10.

people.name: Goliath
people.summary: A famous giant of Gath, who for forty days openly defied the armies of Israel, but was at length slain by David with a stone from a sling (1 Sam. 17:4).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of the sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:9).

people.name: Abinadab
people.summary: The second of the eight sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:8).

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: A son of Helon, and chief of the tribe of Zebulun at the time of the census in the wilderness (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Abner
people.summary: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).

places.name: Azekah
places.summary: Dug over, a town in the Shephelah or low hills of Judah (Josh. 15:35), where the five confederated Amoritish kings were defeated by Joshua and their army destroyed by a hailstrom (10:10, 11).

places.name: Ephes-dammim
places.summary: Boundary of blood, a place in the tribe of Judah where the Philistines encamped when David fought with Goliath (1 Sam. 17:1). It was probably so called as having been the scene of frequent sanguinary conflicts between Israel and the Philistines.

places.name: valley of Elah
places.summary: Valley of, where the Israelites were encamped when David killed Goliath (1 Sam. 17:2, 19). It was near Shochoh of Judah and Azekah (17:1). It is the modern Wady es-Sunt, i.e., “valley of the acacia.”

places.name: Gath
places.summary: A wine-vat, one of the five royal cities of the Philistines (Josh. 13:3) on which the ark brought calamity (1 Sam. 5:8, 9; 6:17). It was famous also as being the birthplace or residence of Goliath (1 Sam. 17:4).

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: A city in the “hill country” of Judah. It was originally called Ephrath (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7; Ruth 4:11). It was also called Beth-lehem Ephratah (Micah 5:2), Beth-lehem-judah (1 Sam. 17:12), and “the city of David” (Luke 2:4).

places.name: Ekron
places.summary: Firm-rooted, the most northerly of the five towns belonging to the lords of the Philistines, about 11 miles north of Gath. It was assigned to Judah (Josh. 13:3), and afterwards to Dan (19:43), but came again into the full possession of the Philistines (1 Sam. 5:10).

places.name: Shaaraim
places.summary: A city in the plain of Judah (1 Sam. 17:52); called also Sharaim (Josh. 15:36).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Reign of Saul
events.summary: Passage: 1 Samuel 10:1–31:2. People: Saul. Lasted about 40 years.
